title: BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook immutable dispatcher binding strands accrued debt if NFTMinterV2.replaceDispatcher is used
description: The hook's `dispatcher` is `immutable` and is the only address authorized to call `onDispatch`. Meanwhile, NFTMinterV2 (src/V2/NFTMinterV2.sol:227-247) has `replaceDispatcher(index, newDispatcher)` which swaps the dispatcher registered under a given index. Intended flow when replacing a BalancerPoolerV2: (1) owner deploys new BalancerPoolerV2, (2) owner deploys new MintDebtHook bound to the new BalancerPoolerV2, (3) owner calls NFTMinterV2.replaceDispatcher(index, newBalancerPoolerV2) and `newBalancerPoolerV2.setHook(newMintDebtHook)`. The OLD hook continues to hold the already-accrued `mintDebt` and can be pulled via `pull()` — that value is NOT lost. But: the OLD BalancerPoolerV2 is now decoupled from NFTMinterV2 (no future dispatches flow through it), and if the old BalancerPoolerV2 is re-used in any other wiring the old hook's `dispatcher` check effectively permanently pins it to that one dispatcher. There is no migration path to move debt between hooks, and there is no `setDispatcher` on the hook. A more subtle concern: while the hook's dispatcher is immutable, the dispatcher's `hook` is mutable (ATokenDispatcherV2.setHook). If the owner calls `setHook(newHook)` on BalancerPoolerV2 before calling `pull()`, the OLD hook still works to pull accrued debt (good), but any further dispatch through BalancerPoolerV2 accrues debt on the NEW hook. This splits historical debt across two hook contracts and complicates accounting/monitoring.
impact: Operational risk during dispatcher or hook replacement: previously-accrued debt stays on the old hook and must be pulled separately before or after the rotation. A distracted rotation could leave debt stranded on an orphaned hook. No fund loss (owner / recipient can always pull from the old hook), but accounting is split across contracts that look indistinguishable from the outside.
recommendation: Either (a) add a one-shot `transferDebt(address newHook)` function restricted to owner that forwards `mintDebt` state to a successor hook (callable only by owner, only when `mintDebt > 0`, and only once); or (b) document the replacement runbook explicitly (call `pull()` on the old hook to zero its debt before calling `setHook` on the dispatcher); or (c) make `dispatcher` settable by the owner with an event, removing the immutable binding while keeping the msg.sender check enforced against the current stored value.
